context: Mobile-only Expo React Native parental-control app with Supabase-first backend and FastAPI support where needed.

phase_1_discovery.audience: Parents and guardians managing multiple children or monitored devices; secondary audience is children and teens receiving clear, respectful limits.
success_actions: See family status at a glance
Pair a device by code or QR
Set and edit a device limit
phase_1_discovery.emotional_tone: Calm authority: reassuring, warm, dependable, never surveillance-heavy or punitive.
phase_1_discovery.theme: Light-first with an optional dark mode. Use warm paper surfaces and a deep ink navigation surface; avoid cold generic SaaS styling.
phase_1_discovery.content_strategy: Lead with what needs attention now, then explain usage trends, then expose controls. Use plain Spanish copy and concrete times rather than abstract scores.

references.name: Google Family Link
descriptors: Task-centered tabs for Screen Time and Controls

references.name: Nintendo Switch Parental Controls
descriptors: Daily activity history and monthly summary
Clear distinction between notification and enforcement

phase_2_research.decision: Borrow the clarity and task grouping from Family Link, the explicit enforcement states from Nintendo, and the approachable overview pattern from curated dashboard work; differentiate with an editorial, warm, card-light system.

typography.font_loading: Use expo-google-fonts or the project's existing font strategy; never use Inter for headings.

rules.h1: 36px mobile / 48px large, tight tracking, font weight 700
rules.label: 12px uppercase, letter spacing 2px
rules.numbers: IBM Plex Mono for durations, limits, codes and metrics

colors.archetype: Organic & Earthy with Swiss functional accents
colors.contrast: Use ink on paper/surface; white on forest/terracotta. Verify normal text at 4.5:1 and controls at 3:1.

layouts.navigation: Every screen has a visible solid or opaque glass header with TimeGuard wordmark, current family/profile context and a primary action. Parent bottom tabs: Resumen, Actividad, Controles, Ajustes. Child mode uses a simpler header and one clear request action.
layouts.dashboard: Mobile-first vertical flow: family switcher overline, urgent alert strip, dominant today usage ring, horizontally scrollable device status rail, 7-day usage chart, app breakdown, recent activity. Left-align all copy.
layouts.grid: Use a 2-column asymmetric grid where space permits: primary usage module spans 2 columns, alert/action modules span 1, app list spans 2. On narrow devices collapse to one column. Keep 24px outer padding and 16px internal gaps.
layouts.pairing: A focused step flow: choose monitored role, show 6-character code and QR, explain expiration, confirmation state, then device nickname/profile. Never bury code expiry.
layouts.controls: Segmented profile/device selector, limit row with duration, schedule rows, allow/deny app list, block toggle, and save action. Flat surfaces with 1px borders; no excessive cards.
layouts.lock_screen: Monitored-device mode uses a warm solid background, large remaining/renewal message, friendly illustration-free typography, and a single Request more time button. Do not imply the child can bypass enforcement.

component_path: Use JavaScript files under /app/frontend/app and /app/frontend/src/components; do not provide TSX-only implementation guidance. Prefer existing Expo Router and React Native primitives; use existing UI primitives when available.
visual_enhancers: Subtle paper grain via a low-opacity tiled texture or CSS/native overlay; decorative only and aria-hidden equivalent where applicable
Thin rules and offset labels inspired by editorial print
Layered ambient shadows only on floating sheets
Small status dots with text labels; never color alone
Avoid gradients except a tiny chart-area tint if necessary

motion.entrance: Stagger dashboard sections by 40ms with opacity and translateY
motion.interactions: Press scale 0.98 and explicit color transitions on buttons, tabs and list rows
motion.realtime: Pulse the status dot once when a Supabase device update arrives; do not loop indefinitely
motion.loading: Use skeleton blocks with a calm shimmer
motion.reduced_motion: Respect prefers-reduced-motion / AccessibilityInfo and remove stagger, pulse and shimmer when requested
motion.implementation: Animate opacity and transform only; never use transition: all. Use React Native Animated or Reanimated if already installed.

supabase_data_model.realtime: Subscribe to devices, device_sessions, device_limits and extra_time_requests scoped to the family
supabase_data_model.rls: Every table must enforce family membership through auth.uid(); parents can manage family children/devices, monitored profiles can read their own lock/request state, and no user can access another family.
supabase_data_model.client_rules: Use a single Supabase client utility, loading/error/empty states, optimistic UI only with rollback, and never place service-role keys in Expo.

api_and_platform.expo: Portrait mobile app targeting Android phone and AndroidTV-friendly monitored UI
api_and_platform.fastapi: Use only for server-side integrations that cannot safely run in the client; keep Supabase as source of truth
api_and_platform.native_measurement: Real other-app measurement and device blocking require Android native permissions/services (UsageStatsManager, accessibility/device-admin or managed-device approach) and a development build; clearly show unavailable permission states in MVP.
api_and_platform.mocked: If native usage measurement or blocking is not connected during MVP testing, label those flows as SIMULATED in the UI and keep data writes structurally compatible with Supabase.

accessibility: All buttons, links, inputs, tabs, menus, alerts, metrics, requests and confirmation states include data-testid in kebab-case
Use accessible labels and roles for icons and controls
Never communicate status by color alone
Support large font sizes and dynamic type without clipping
Announce realtime limit changes and request approval status
Use a native accessible QR/code presentation and copy-code action

media.guidance: Do not add stock photography; the product is about private family data. Prefer type, linework and subtle texture. Never use placeholder image URLs.

3d_libraries.reason: This is a trust and clarity product; 3D would compete with actionable data. Use native 2D charts and lightweight SVG only.

general_ui_ux_design_guidelines: Use generous 24px screen padding and 32px section spacing
Do not center the app container or all content
Headers must have an opaque background; never complete transparent surfaces over content
Use rounded corners sparingly at 12px for sheets and 8px for controls
Use Sonner/toast equivalent for feedback where supported, with an inline fallback
Every async state has loading, success, error and empty treatment
Use Spanish labels such as Resumen, Tiempo de pantalla, Dispositivos, Límites, Pedir más tiempo
Do not use AI-assistant emojis as icons
Do not hide core desktop/web links behind a hamburger; this is mobile-only, so use bottom tabs and a compact header
Never use placeholder content or fake logos
instructions_to_main_agent: Build the first screen as a useful authenticated family dashboard, not a splash image. Preserve Expo Router conventions, use .js files for new implementation guidance, wire Supabase early, add RLS migrations/configuration, and attach data-testid to every interactive and key informational element. Keep parent and monitored-device flows visually distinct while sharing tokens.
